task.title: Cancel durable workflow runs with exact caller-owned reasons
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/694 under decision https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/693 by persisting terminal caller-controlled cancellation against an exact run revision without rewriting workflow topology.
acceptance_criteria: Validate and preserve one non-empty exact cancellation reason for a non-terminal, non-cancelled run.
Require the caller-observed revision and append one event carrying exact current-phase provenance.
Expose cancellation separately from workflow-authored terminal state while rejecting every later lifecycle event.
Reject stale, duplicate, terminal, malformed, and phase-inconsistent cancellation fail closed across reopen.

attempts.summary: Established RED cancellation lifecycle and replay coverage.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused workflow_run_store suite failed because cancellation reason values, store mutation, projected cancellation state, and typed lifecycle errors did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for exact reason preservation, revision increments, stale and racing callers, terminal and duplicate cancellation, reopen projection, and malformed provenance.

attempts.diagnostic: Keeping cancellation distinct from authored terminal phases preserved topology semantics while making cancellation terminal for caller-controlled execution.
attempts.patch: Added validated cancellation reasons, version-one cancellation events, exact-revision mutation, strict replay projection, ADR-0011, and lifecycle documentation.

attempts.summary: Deferred a shared mutation-helper refactor identified by review.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found duplicated load, revision-check, append, and concurrency-error mapping between advance and cancel, but classified it as a trivial maintainability nit rather than a behavioral defect.
attempts.patch: Merged the verified bounded behavior; later pause and resume work introduced shared revision and append helpers, leaving complete adoption as an explicit follow-up observation.

outcome.summary: A durable workflow run can now be cancelled exactly once with preserved caller rationale and phase provenance while all later history fails closed.

lessons: Caller cancellation and workflow-authored terminal phases are separate semantics and should remain separately projected.
A cancellation event needs exact phase provenance so replay can reject impossible histories against immutable topology.
Cancellation is terminal for caller-controlled lifecycle even though it does not rewrite the authored current phase.
Repeated exact-revision mutation patterns should converge on shared concurrency mapping as lifecycle operations grow.
Cancellation persists rationale but grants no execution, retry, compensation, provider, tool, scheduling, or permission authority.
